topics.definition: A Stack is a linear data structure following the Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) principle where elements are inserted and deleted from the top.
topics.algorithm: Push: stack[top++] = x; Pop: return stack[--top]; Peek: return stack[top-1].
topics.complexity: Push: O(1), Pop: O(1), Peek: O(1), Search: O(n).
topics.example: Call stack in operating systems, undo-redo operations in text editors, bracket balancing.
topics.summary: Stack provides O(1) insertion and removal at one end obeying LIFO ordering.

topics.definition: A Queue is a linear data structure following the First-In-First-Out (FIFO) principle where elements are inserted at the rear and removed from the front.
topics.algorithm: Enqueue: queue[rear++] = x; Dequeue: return queue[front++]; Peek: return queue[front].
topics.complexity: Enqueue: O(1), Dequeue: O(1), Search: O(n).
topics.example: CPU task scheduling, print spooling, breadth-first search traversal.
topics.summary: Queue regulates ordered task dispatch obeying FIFO ordering.

topics.definition: A Binary Tree is a hierarchical non-linear tree data structure in which each node has at most two children referred to as the left child and right child.
topics.algorithm: Traversal: Inorder (Left, Root, Right), Preorder (Root, Left, Right), Postorder (Left, Right, Root).
topics.complexity: Search/Insert/Delete: O(log n) in balanced binary search tree, O(n) in skewed tree.
topics.example: Expression parsing trees, Huffman coding compression, hierarchical file system representations.
topics.summary: Binary trees structure hierarchical relationships with logarithmic access in balanced configurations.

topics.definition: Time Complexity quantifies the computational execution time required by an algorithm as a mathematical function of input size n.
topics.algorithm: Count dominant primitive operations; express growth rate discarding lower-order terms and constant coefficients.
topics.complexity: O(1) Constant < O(log n) Logarithmic < O(n) Linear < O(n log n) Linearithmic < O(n^2) Quadratic < O(2^n) Exponential.
topics.example: Binary search has O(log n) complexity; Merge sort has O(n log n) complexity; Bubble sort has O(n^2) complexity.
topics.summary: Big-O notation provides a deterministic upper bound on algorithmic execution time.
